summary: Service-account CLI token exchange failing with 'invalid_grant' after Okta session-lifetime policy update
description:
Issue summary:
Service-account CLI users began receiving 'invalid_grant' errors when exchanging an OIDC device flow code for an access token. The failures started immediately after we rolled out a revised Okta session-lifetime policy on 2026-03-10 morning maintenance window.

Impact:
- Several internal automation jobs that use service-account CLI tokens (backup export, infra snapshots, and some scheduled analytics) are failing to authenticate.
- No data leakage suspected; requests are rejected at token issuance.
- Impacted services: backup-exporter, infra-snap-scheduler, analytics-cron.

Environment:
- Okta tenant: redwood-corp.okta.com
- Auth proxy: auth-proxy-01/02 (ecs cluster redwood-auth-prod, us-east)
- Affected clients: redwood-cli v0.9.12 (service-account flow), internal CI runners using service principals.

Steps to reproduce:
1) redwood-cli auth login --service-account --device
2) Follow device code / open URL; complete SSO flow as service principal
3) CLI attempts token exchange: POST /oauth2/v1/token with grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code
4) Response: HTTP 400 {"error":"invalid_grant","error_description":"The provided authorization grant (e.g., device code) is invalid, expired, or revoked."}

Observed logs / errors:
- auth-proxy logs (2026-03-10T09:17:12Z): "token-exchange failed: invalid_grant: token_expired_or_clock_skew"
- Okta logs (query id: 0oab1xA2Y3): device_code issued at 2026-03-10T09:16:22Z, token request at 2026-03-10T09:17:12Z, Okta returned invalid_grant with message: "Session policy prevents token issuance due to session_lifespan change"
- NTP offsets: auth-proxy-02 drift +5s on 2026-03-10 before drift correction.

Temporary workaround:
- Re-triggering the device flow immediately after the policy rollback used during the window allowed a small percentage of exchanges to succeed.
- For automation jobs, we manually switched to a short-lived machine identity token issued by the infra-team (mitigates immediate production impact but is not long-term).

Notes:
- The issue is reproducible against prod Okta only. Staging unaffected.
- No indication of compromised credentials; likely a session/TTL mismatch between Okta policy and our token validation/rotation logic.
comments: 2026-03-10 10:04 - Support (Ava Thompson): Ticket opened after backup-exporter alert (SRE) reports repeated 400 invalid_grant errors during scheduled run. Notified #platform-auth and paged on-call.

2026-03-10 10:18 - SRE (Liam Chen): Observed token-exchange failures from auth-proxy-01 and -02. Confirmed Okta admin changed sessionLifetimeMinutes from 60->15 in a policy patch at 2026-03-10T09:15Z. Rolling back to previous value restored some success rates.

2026-03-10 12:22 - Auth Eng (Riya Patel): Collected Okta system logs and replayed device flow. Okta's response includes policy enforcement note. Hypothesis: our auth-proxy caches a device_code expiry or expects a longer session TTL when performing server-side exchange. Also noticed auth-proxy's SESSION_TTL env set to 3600 while Okta now 900s.

2026-03-11 08:37 - SRE (Ethan Ruiz): Reproduced locally. auth-proxy returned invalid_grant when device_code issued just before policy change window. Confirmed NTP drift on auth-proxy-02 (+5s) but not enough to justify the failure alone. Adding clock correction reduced flakiness but did not fully resolve.

2026-03-12 09:03 - Auth Eng (Riya Patel): Deployed hotfix to auth-proxy that reads Okta session policy during token validation and enforces shorter TTL for new device codes. Will monitor for 24 hours.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: Okta session_lifespan policy changed during issuance-to-exchange window causing Okta to reject token requests that span policy boundaries.

Confirmed: Okta admin event at 2026-03-10T09:15Z updated sessionLifetimeMinutes for the default policy causing newly-issued device codes to be considered invalid when exchanged after a policy enforcement timestamp.

Auth-proxy configuration mismatch: SESSION_TTL was hard-coded to 3600s; Okta policy reduced to 900s. The proxy did not query Okta policy at exchange time and assumed the longer TTL when validating device_code expiry locally.
NTP clock skew on auth-proxy-02 contributed to timing edge cases but was not the root cause.
Repro steps validated by re-issuing a device_code immediately before and after simulated policy change; exchanges after policy change failed consistently unless auth-proxy TTL aligned with Okta.
Related components to review: auth-proxy token cache, device-flow handler, Okta policy change procedures (should coordinate with Platform Auth).
resolution: Hotfix deployed to auth-proxy to dynamically read Okta session policy at token-exchange time and use Okta-provided TTL for device_code validation. Also rolled back the Okta session_lifetime change during investigation to reduce customer impact. Follow-ups: (1) Add a pre-change coordination step in the Okta policy runbook, (2) add automated end-to-end test exercising device flow against policy change window, (3) add NTP monitoring to critical auth instances. Pending: monitoring for 24h to declare 'Resolved'.
next_steps: Monitor token-exchange success rate for 48h and confirm backup-exporter and cron jobs return to normal.
Add an OKTA_POLICY_SYNC job in infra to surface policy drift and env mismatches to SRE.alerts.
Postmortem draft to be created in Confluence by 2026-03-15 (owner: Riya Patel).
